q: A blown $10\,\text{A}$ fuse is replaced with a $16\,\text{A}$ fuse. Why is that dangerous even though the electricity works?
a: The circuit cable is dimensioned for a current of $10\,\text{A}$. A larger fuse lets through a current of up to $16\,\text{A}$, and then the thermal power of the conductors, $P = RI^2$, is $(16 : 10)^2 \approx 2.6$ times as large. The cable and the connections can overheat, the insulation can be damaged and a fire can start.

q: May a layperson install a new socket in a wall in Finland? Name two electrical jobs that a layperson may do themselves.
a: No: electrical installation work belongs to electrical professionals. A layperson may, for example, replace a fuse and a lamp, reset a tripped circuit breaker or residual current device (RCD) and repair an extension cord. An up-to-date list is on the website of Tukes.
